title: Fast screen: remove redundant procedural prompt lines
hypothesis: The existing workflow-lite prompt lets Astra solve coding tasks faster while preserving verification, safety, planner and tool contracts.
falsified_if: The prompt transform fails activation or the screen loses correctness; weak or mixed latency evidence parks the candidate rather than proving a universal negative.
local_evidence: The earlier workflow pilot was incomplete and exposed a now-fixed edit newline defect; it produced no valid promotion decision. The user explicitly requested faster experimentation. This fresh paired six-run screen uses the current fixed tools and exact audited nine-line prompt deletion; it does not reuse historical controls or combine tool-scope/effort changes.

task_suffixes.simple_prompt: This task is self-contained; do not browse or use external network services.
task_suffixes.failure_recovery: File scope: change only shipping/quotes.py. Do not add files. This task is self-contained; do not browse or use external network services.
task_suffixes.multifile_order_cancellation: File scope: change only orders/__init__.py, orders/api.py, orders/models.py, orders/repository.py and orders/service.py. Do not add files. This task is self-contained; do not browse or use external network services.

deterministic_outcomes: exact prompt transform and unchanged serialized tool schemas
decision_rule: Seed 917. Six screen-only runs: one per arm on simple_prompt and two coding tasks. Simple control first, coding-task order randomized, arm order randomized within adjacent pairs. No duplicate smoke/pilot collection. Maximum six launches, $1.75 between-run standard-equivalent estimated cost threshold (one-run overshoot possible), 360 active worker seconds. Stop immediately after a task or protocol/activation failure; preserve its resource accounting. Exclude arithmetic from the coding speed comparison but include all spend. Advance to a fresh small replication only if all runs pass, aggregate coding latency is at least 10% lower, and neither coding task is more than 10% slower. Otherwise park the candidate with its observed tradeoffs; one run per task cannot establish a universal failure or success. A positive screen can only justify further testing, never production promotion or a long-task claim. No defaults change.
